\section[\texorpdfstring{\ar{عطل} (ʿuṭl)}{عطل (ʿuṭl)}]{\ar{عطل} (ʿuṭl) — a breakdown; a fault}

\label{lesson:AR-C460-utl}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Arabic for purchases, then the Arabic for to economise.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ar{عطل}}
\textbf{\ar{عطل}} — \emph{ʿuṭl} — \textquotedblleft{}a breakdown; a fault\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ar{كان} \ar{في} \ar{السيارة} \ar{عطل} \ar{صغير}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{kāna fī as-sayyāra ʿuṭl ṣaghīr.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The car had a small fault.
\end{quote}

Plural: \ar{أعطال}, \emph{aʿṭāl}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ar{عطل}} (\emph{ʿuṭl}) is built on the native Arabic root \emph{ʿ-ṭ-l}, \textquotedblleft{}to be idle, without work\textquotedblright{} (Lane).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for getting around.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{ʿuṭl}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{ʿuṭl}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{kāna fī as-sayyāra ʿuṭl ṣaghīr.} — The car had a small fault.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Arabic for purchases, then the Arabic for to economise, then say \emph{ʿuṭl} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \ar{عطل} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}A breakdown; a fault\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\ar{انكسر} (inkasara)}{انكسر (inkasara)}]{\ar{انكسر} (inkasara) — to get broken}

\label{lesson:AR-C460-inkasara}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Arabic for a breakdown, then the Arabic for a malfunction.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ar{انكسر}}
\textbf{\ar{انكسر}} — \emph{inkasara} — \textquotedblleft{}to get broken\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ar{انكسرت} \ar{نظارتي} \ar{في} \ar{الطريق}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{inkasarat naẓẓāratī fī aṭ-ṭarīq.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
My glasses got broken on the way.
\end{quote}

Present: \ar{ينكسر}, \emph{yankasir}.

\emph{kasara} breaks a thing; \emph{inkasara} is what the thing does.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ar{انكسر}} (\emph{inkasara}) is built on the native Arabic root \emph{k-s-r}, \textquotedblleft{}to break\textquotedblright{} (Lane). It is Form VII, \textquotedblleft{}to be broken\textquotedblright{}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for getting around.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{inkasara}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{inkasara}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{inkasarat naẓẓāratī fī aṭ-ṭarīq.} — My glasses got broken on the way.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Arabic for a breakdown, then the Arabic for a malfunction, then say \emph{inkasara} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]

\end{tcolorbox}

\label{lesson:AR-C460-talifa}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Arabic for a malfunction, then the Arabic for to get broken.

Before the new one: say the Arabic for to get broken, then the Arabic for to go bad.
